canonical_title: The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Canonical record for The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories, PKD's short-story collection. This single archive manifestation runs 403 pages. The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories constitutes Volume 4 of The Collected Stories of Philip K.
page_summary:
The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories is the canonical works record for PKD's short-story collection. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories (Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volume 4) (circa 1954–1964). The archive copy runs 403 pages.

Archive summary: The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories constitutes Volume 4 of The Collected Stories of Philip K.

Researchers can use this entry to trace publication context, later commentary, and relationships to other works.

motifs: Precognition and predictive justice systems, most famously in the title story
Domestic and bureaucratic settings destabilized by encroaching technological control
reading.significance: James Tiptree, Jr.'s introduction -- itself written by one of science fiction's most celebrated writers -- offers a valuable secondary-source characterization of what makes Dick's fiction distinctively strange, and the volume's title story's film adaptation is one of the most commercially successful Dick adaptations to date.
reading.closing_note: This entry documents the anthology as a publishing object; readers seeking analysis of the individual stories, including 'The Minority Report' itself, should consult each story's own dossier.

reading_provenance.note: Close reading of the primary text plus attributed evidence from the archive. Candidate: not yet promoted to canonical.

critical_caution: Most of the individual stories in this volume already have their own dedicated close-reading dossiers elsewhere in this corpus. This entry describes the collection as a publishing object.
